summary: Anthropic is launching a $5 million grant program to fund independent researchers building open-source evaluations of how AI models affect user wellbeing, and is publishing guidance on what makes such evaluations rigorous.

practices.reason: The stated criteria for rigorous wellbeing evaluations (clear pass/fail definitions, expert validation, testing both overcompliance and overrefusal, multi-turn scenario design) give an engineering team concrete guidance for building or assessing their own safety evals, though no instrument itself is handed over.
practices.quote: we’re seeking evaluations that: State clearly what they are measuring (i.e., what counts as a pass or fail, and why it matters); Involve clinical and subject-matter experts in the design and validation; Test both precautions and harms (i.e., evaluate the risk of both overcompliance and overrefusal); Reflect how users actually use AI (often, this means constructing scenarios that represent multi-turn conversations, where risk escalates and context shifts over the course of a long conversation); Validate their graders against real subject-matter experts.
